docs.title: ComplexEnchants
docs.text:
Custom enchantments for Paper, defined in YAML and registered as real Minecraft enchantments. Use them the classic way (drag a book onto an item, with success and destroy chances) or the vanilla way (enchanting table, anvil, villagers, loot), switchable globally or per enchantment.

Enchantments can also do things: damage bonuses, potions, area mining, auto-smelt, permanent speed and more, with triggers, conditions, chances, cooldowns and per-level formulas. That part has its own guide: Effects.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Enchantments are real registry enchantments: they show in the vanilla tooltip, make items glow, work with /enchant and are returned by ItemStack#getEnchantments().
  • Two modes, global and per enchantment:
  • BOOKS: drag books onto items, with success and destroy chances, plus an extractor, a catalyst, a transmuter (each of a rarity or generic) and a slot expander.
  • VANILLA: enchanting table, anvil, grindstone, librarian trades, chest loot and fishing.
  • Enchantment slots per item group, with slot expanders.
  • Lore rendered in packets: players see a formatted list (sorted by rarity, with descriptions) while the real item stays clean. An ITEM mode writes the lore into items for plugins that read it.
  • Menus (menus/): enchantment lists by rarity (with a button to filter them by item), enchantment details and a shop selling random books by rarity for money (Vault) or experience. No menu plugin needed; PlaceholderAPI works if installed.
  • In-game editor (/ce editor): create and edit enchantments, their effects, rarities, item groups and vanilla enchantments with chest menus and Minecraft's dialogs (more).
  • Ready to play: 112 enchantments, 7 rarities and their menus come with the plugin (installed on the first start; see Installation).
  • Deleted enchantments never break items: they stay registered as "tombstones".
  • No required dependencies. Vault (money in menus) and PlaceholderAPI (placeholders in menus, and our own placeholders) are optional.
  • Effects: 32 triggers, 51 conditions and 55 effects (combat, tools, passives, utility), all reloadable with /ce reload. See Effects.
  • Folia supported.
  • All messages in MiniMessage, with English and Spanish included. /ce help lists the commands each player can use.
  • Clear configuration errors: file, key, what was expected and what was used instead. A broken file never stops the others from loading.

docs.title: Enchantments API
docs.text:
The api module has no dependency on the rest of the plugin.

ComplexEnchantsApi api = Bukkit.getServicesManager().load(ComplexEnchantsApi.class);

api.enchant("life_bolt").ifPresent(enchant -> {
    ApplyResult result = api.apply(player, item, enchant.key(), 2, ApplyCause.API);
    if (!result.isSuccess()) {
        player.sendMessage("Could not apply: " + result.status());
    }
});
Map<CustomEnchant, Integer> onItem = api.enchantsOn(item);
api.openShop(player);
api.openMenu(player, "enchant_list", "epic");

Cancellable events, so protection, claim and clan plugins can intervene:

Event When EnchantApplyEvent Before any custom enchantment is applied (book, anvil, table, command, API) EnchantRemoveEvent Before one is removed (extractor, command, API) BookPurchaseEvent Before a [buy] purchase (the shop) is charged. The price can be changed (discounts) BookTransmuteEvent Before a transmuter is used on a book. The chance can be changed EnchantEffectEvent Before an effect runs (for example, to stop effects between clan allies) ComplexEnchantsReloadEvent After every successful /ce reload (not cancellable)

Custom effects, conditions and triggers: see the API section of Effects.

Every listener uses ignoreCancelled = true, so if your plugin cancels a click or event, ComplexEnchants does nothing. Methods that change items must be called on the thread that owns them (the main thread on Paper, the region thread on Folia).

docs.title: Effects API
docs.text:
ComplexEnchantsEffects effects = Bukkit.getServicesManager().load(ComplexEnchantsEffects.class);

effects.registerEffect(new CustomEffect() {
    public String id() { return "myplugin:fireball"; }
    public List<EffectArgument> arguments() { return List.of(EffectArgument.number("speed", 1.0)); }
    public void execute(EffectContext context) {
        context.player().launchProjectile(Fireball.class)
                .setVelocity(context.player().getLocation().getDirection().multiply(context.number("speed")));
    }
});
effects.registerCondition(myCondition);                 // "myplugin:in_clan_territory: true"
effects.registerTrigger("myplugin:dash", true);         // then: effects.fireTrigger(player, "myplugin:dash", event, target)
  • Your ids need a namespace (myplugin:…), so they never clash with the built-in ones.
  • Register them in onEnable. The first effects load waits for the server's first tick, when every plugin has registered its own; registering later reloads the effects automatically.
  • Your effects get the same validation, chance, cooldown, conditions and levels as built-in ones.
  • EnchantEffectEvent (cancellable) is fired right before any effect runs, with the player, the enchantment, the effect, the trigger, the level and the targets. Cancel it (for example, between clan allies) and the effect doesn't run nor start its cooldown. It's only created if some plugin listens to it.
  • ComplexEnchantsReloadEvent is fired after every successful /ce reload.

docs.title: Commands and permissions
docs.text:
Main command /complexenchants, alias /ce. Players only see the subcommands they have permission for.

Command Permission Default /ce help (or /ce): the commands you can use, clickable; menus' own commands included complexenchants.command.help everyone /ce shop complexenchants.shop everyone /ce shop <player> complexenchants.shop.others op /ce menu open <menu> [player] [argument] [page], /ce menu list complexenchants.command.menu op /ce debug (see which of your effects run, or why not) complexenchants.command.debug op /ce give skillbook <players> [amount] (the active skills book) complexenchants.command.give op /ce list [page] complexenchants.command.list op /ce info <enchant> (also minecraft:sharpness) complexenchants.command.info op /ce reload complexenchants.command.reload op /ce enchant <enchant> [level] complexenchants.command.enchant op /ce unenchant <enchant> complexenchants.command.enchant op /ce item (slots and enchantments of the held item) complexenchants.command.item op /ce give book <players> <enchant> [level] [success] complexenchants.command.give op /ce give random <players> [rarity\|any] (without a rarity: any enchantment, by weight) complexenchants.command.give op /ce give extractor\|catalyst\|transmuter <players> [amount] [rarity\|any] [value] complexenchants.command.give op /ce give slot-expander <players> [amount] complexenchants.command.give op /ce editor (create and edit enchantments, rarities, item groups and vanilla enchantments in game) complexenchants.editor op

complexenchants.admin grants every permission above. The texts of /ce help are in the lang files (command.help). /ce enchant and /ce unenchant act on the item in the main hand and follow the same rules as everything else (applicable items, conflicts, slots).

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text:
• Protection and claim plugins: respected through cancelled events and the API events above.
  • Plugins that read item lore (some shops and auction houses) see items without the enchantment lines in PACKETS mode. That's expected; use ITEM mode if you need them.
  • Bedrock players (Geyser): enchantments work, since they are real enchantments. The formatted lore is sent in packets like any other lore and usually shows, but Geyser translates items in its own way, so how it looks on Bedrock is not guaranteed. ComplexEnchants does not depend on Geyser or Floodgate.
  • Archaeology (suspicious sand and gravel) is not filtered: if an enchantment is allowed in loot or fishing, it may appear there. Its tag is shared with loot and Minecraft gives no event to separate it.

docs.title: Performance and profiling
docs.text:
ComplexEnchants is event-driven: it runs no repeating tasks, except the interval trigger and bleed, and only for players who have them. Effects are compiled when loading, so nothing is parsed in game, and a player without effects is skipped in the first check of every event. The only work that happens all the time is adding the lore to inventory packets, which runs on the network threads (not the main thread):

  • Before copying an item, a quick check skips everything without custom enchantments, including items with only vanilla enchantments (unless you gave them a name, rarity or visible description in vanilla-enchants.yml) or lore from other plugins.
  • Formatted lore is cached per set of enchantments and cleared on /ce reload. A cache hit costs well under a microsecond; building a new entry takes about a quarter of a millisecond, once per combination.
  • PlaceholderAPI placeholders are cheap enough for TAB or a scoreboard refreshing every few ticks: a few microseconds each. Values that don't depend on the player (enchant_…, count, rarity_…) and the lookup of enchantments by name are computed once per configuration.

docs.title: Measuring it on your server with spark
docs.text:
spark is the standard profiler for Paper.

  1. Install spark (or use the built-in /spark on recent Paper builds).
  2. At a busy time, start a profile that includes the network threads, where the lore is rendered: 
    /spark profiler start --thread * --timeout 600
  3. Let players play normally for 10 minutes. The profile stops on its own and spark posts a link.
  4. Open the link and search for complexenchants:
  5. Server thread: listeners (clicks, anvil, table, loot) and effects: TriggerListener and Dispatcher (triggered effects), PassiveManager (passives, only when equipment changes) and ToolBreak (area and vein mining). This should be a tiny fraction of a millisecond per tick. If ToolBreak stands out, lower tools.max-blocks or the radius of your area effects; if Dispatcher does, look for effects with target: nearby and a large radius on frequent triggers.
  6. Netty threads: DisplayHandler and ItemDisplay (lore). This does not affect TPS, but it should stay a small share of those threads.
  7. Placeholders: PapiExpansion and Placeholders appear under whichever thread asks for them (the server thread, or TAB's and scoreboard plugins' own threads). Each call should take a few microseconds.
  8. Menus: MenuService and MenuRenderer, only when a menu is opened or clicked.
  9. To compare, run the same profile once with display.mode: ITEM (no packet work at all).

If ComplexEnchants shows up high, please share the spark link in your report.

docs.title: Building from source
docs.text:
Requires JDK 25 (Gradle downloads it automatically if missing). The .jar runs on Java 21.

./gradlew build                 # jar in plugin/build/libs/, runs every test
./gradlew :plugin:runServer     # test server, Paper 1.21.11
./gradlew :plugin:runServer26   # test server, Paper 26.3

Modules: api (public API), core (all logic, Paper API only), effects (the effects module, Effects), nms/v1_21 and nms/v26_3 (packet display per Minecraft version) and plugin (packaging). Tests use JUnit and MockBukkit; a skipped test fails the build, so a green build means every test really ran.

docs.title: FAQ
docs.text:
I added an enchantment and it doesn't exist. New enchantments need a server restart. /ce list shows "pending restart".

I changed max-level and nothing happened. Registry changes need a restart. /ce reload lists what is still waiting.

Can I delete an enchantment? Prefer enabled: false. If you delete the file, it stays registered as a tombstone so items keep working, and its lore shows it as removed.

The console says known-enchants.yml was damaged. ComplexEnchants recovered every id it could find in it and kept a copy named known-enchants.yml.damaged-<time>. Check that no enchantment is missing.

Players see the vanilla enchantment line too. Set display.hide-vanilla-enchant-lines: true.

Menu items that cost MONEY can't be paid. Install Vault and an economy plugin, then restart.

The console says a file is not saved as UTF-8. It was edited with a program that saved it in another encoding (old Windows Notepad does, as "ANSI"). It is still read, but accents may look wrong: open it and save it as UTF-8. Until then, new options are not added to it.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
Server Java Paper 1.21.11 (or a fork such as Purpur) 21 Paper 26.3 25 Folia (same versions) same

Spigot is not supported: it has no supported way to register enchantments.

Optional: Vault plus an economy plugin (EssentialsX, CMI…), only for menu items that cost money; PlaceholderAPI, for its placeholders in menus and for ComplexEnchants' own placeholders.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
1. Put ComplexEnchants.jar in plugins/ and start the server once.
  2. Default files are created in plugins/ComplexEnchants/. Existing files are never overwritten.
  3. Add your enchantments to plugins/ComplexEnchants/enchants/ (see below) and restart.

What comes with the plugin. On the first start (when there is no enchants/ folder yet) you get 112 ready-made enchantments (combat, tools, armour, bows, tridents, maces, spears, elytra, totems, fishing…), 7 rarities (simple, special, rare, epic and legendary, mythic, abyssal), item groups, the helper items and the menus. Rarities up to epic use VANILLA mode (table, anvil, villagers, loot, fishing); legendary and above are BOOKS-only, so they come from the shop, commands or rewards. Change or delete anything: a deleted enchantment or menu never comes back (only enchants/_example.yml, the template, is restored if missing). Never delete an enchantment that players already have: set enabled: false instead.

docs.title: Reload or restart?
docs.text:
Minecraft only accepts new enchantments while the server is starting. So:

  • /ce reload applies: names, descriptions, colours, lore format, rarities (display), book chances, source switches, slots, helper items, the visual options of vanilla-enchants.yml, menus and messages (except a menu's own command:).
  • A restart is needed to: add an enchantment, or change its max level, weight, applicable items, conflicts, anvil/table cost, or whether it appears in the table/villagers/loot.

/ce reload tells you exactly which changes are still waiting for a restart. Every option in the default files is marked with ⟳ (reload) or ⏻ (restart).

docs.title: Configuration files
docs.text:
File What it contains config.yml Mode, vanilla mechanics switches, book failure, slots, display, language, how damage effects combine (damage), tool limits (tools) rarities.yml Rarities: name, colour, weight, lore order, default book chances vanilla-enchants.yml Minecraft's enchantments: name, rarity, description and gameplay options (more) item-groups.yml Groups of items (swords, armor…) using items, tags (#minecraft:swords) or other groups (@tools) items.yml Extractor, catalyst, slot expander and transmuter (look of the rarity ones and the generic ones), and the look of books menus/*.yml Menus: the shop, enchantment lists and details, or your own (more) enchants/*.yml One file per enchantment lang/en.yml, lang/es.yml Every message (MiniMessage). Missing keys fall back to the bundled English text data/known-enchants.yml Internal list of every enchantment ever registered. Do not edit backups/ Copies of your files from before new options were added to them (the last 5 of each)

New options after an update. On startup and with /ce reload, the options that a new version adds to config.yml, items.yml and lang/*.yml are added to your files, with their comments and in their place. Nothing you already have changes (values, comments, order); a copy of the previous file goes to backups/. An option is not added if it would change what the plugin does (for example, a vanilla-mechanics switch whose default depends on the mode), nor inside a section written on one line (display: {mode: ITEM}): the console says so once. Your content files (rarities, item groups, vanilla-enchants.yml, enchantments, menus) are never touched. Turn it off with update-files: false.

docs.title: Menus and shop
docs.text:
Menus are files in menus/ (the file name is the menu id). They know about enchantments, so you need no menu plugin and no placeholders per slot: a list of enchantments fills its slots and pages by itself. Everything is applied with /ce reload, except adding or changing a menu's own command: (restart).

Four menus are installed with a new menus/ folder (a menu you delete never comes back):

Menu What it is shop The shop: random books by rarity. /ce shop opens it enchants Categories: one item per rarity enchant_list Enchantments of a rarity, page by page enchant_info Details of one enchantment

docs.title: A menu
docs.text:
title: "<dark_gray>Enchantments » <rarity> (<page>/<pages>)"
rows: 6                       # 1–6
command: [enchantlist, el]    # optional, own command + aliases (needs a restart)
argument: rarity              # none | rarity | enchant (what the menu receives)
permission: ""                # optional, to open it
disabled-worlds: []
items:
  border:
    slots: [0-9, 17-18, 26-27, 35-36, 44-53]   # or slot: 4
    priority: 10                               # lower wins when items share a slot
    material: black_stained_glass_pane         # or "head:<base64 texture>"
    name: " "                                  # blank name + no lore = no tooltip
  back:
    slot: 49
    material: arrow
    name: "<gray>Back"
    actions: ["[back]"]

Item options: slot/slots, priority, show-if, material, name, lore, amount, item-model, custom-model-data, glint, the click options below. Attributes (damage of a sword…) are never shown.

  • show-if: all must be true for the item to show: previous-page, next-page, permission:<permission>; ! in front negates. If it doesn't show, the next item in that slot does.
  • argument: rarity → opened with a rarity or all (default all); enchant → opened with an enchantment: its id or its name without colours or accents, with spaces or _ (life_bolt, Life Bolt). Own commands take it: /enchantlist [rarity] [page], /enchantinfo <enchantment> (with tab-complete).

docs.title: Enchantment list
docs.text:
enchants:
    type: enchant-list
    slots: [10-16, 19-25, 28-34, 37-43]   # filled in this order; one page = this many
    filter: argument          # argument (the menu's rarity) | all | a rarity id
    sort: RARITY              # RARITY (rarities.yml order, like the lore) | NAME
    vanilla: false            # false | true (ours and vanilla) | only (only vanilla)
    material: enchanted_book
    name: "<name>"
    lore: ["<gray> <description>", "<gray>Max level: <max-level>"]
    overrides:                # only what you write changes
      rarity:
        legendary: { material: nether_star }
      enchant:
        life_bolt: { material: "head:eyJ0ZXh0dXJlcyI6..." }
        "minecraft:mending": { material: experience_bottle }
    actions: ["[open] enchant_info <id>"]

Disabled enchantments are not listed. A list slot without an enchantment (last page) shows what is under it.

Filter by item. filters: in the list is the order of item groups (item-groups.yml) a button goes through with [filter] next / [filter] previous; all = no filter. An enchantment shows up if it can go on any item of the group, so "Helmets" also shows the armour ones, and "Armor" the helmet-only ones. It combines with the menu's rarity, goes back to page 1, and is kept when changing page or coming back with [back]. <filter> (the group's name:, or "All") and <filter-id> work in every item of the menu.

  enchants:
    type: enchant-list
    slots: [10-16, 19-25, 28-34, 37-43]
    filters: [all, helmets, chestplates, leggings, boots, swords, axes, pickaxes, bows]
  filter:
    slot: 46
    material: hopper
    name: "<yellow>Item: <white><filter>"
    left-actions: ["[filter] next"]
    right-actions: ["[filter] previous"]

docs.title: Click actions
docs.text:
actions run with any click; left-actions, right-actions and shift-actions replace them for that click. They run in order:

Action Does [player] <command> The player runs the command (with their permissions) [console] <command> The console runs it [open] <menu> [argument] [page] Opens another menu [back] Back to the previous menu, with its argument and page (closes if there is none) [page] next / [page] previous Page of the enchantment list [filter] next / [filter] previous Item filter of the enchantment list (its filters:) [close], [refresh] Close; draw the menu again [message] <text>, [actionbar] <text> Text to the player [sound] <sound> [volume] [pitch] ui.button.click 1 1.5 [buy] <rarity> Buys a random book of that rarity (the shop)

Opening a menu from another one remembers it for [back]; changing page doesn't. Opening a menu with none open starts again.

docs.title: Cost, permission and confirmation
docs.text:
rare_book:
    slot: 13
    material: enchanted_book
    name: "<rarity> <gray>Book"
    lore: ["<gray>Enchantments: <white><books>", "<gray>Price: <white><cost>"]
    cost: { currency: LEVELS, price: 20 }   # LEVELS, EXP (points) or MONEY (Vault)
    permission: ""                           # optional, to use it
    confirm: false                           # true = confirm first
    deny-actions: ["[message] <red>You need <cost>.", "[sound] entity.villager.no"]
    actions: ["[buy] rare", "[message] <green>Enjoy!"]
confirm:                                     # look of the confirmation (menu level)
  title: "<dark_gray>Confirm purchase"
  accept: { material: lime_stained_glass_pane, name: "<green>Buy for <cost>" }
  cancel: { material: red_stained_glass_pane, name: "<red>Cancel" }
  • The cost is checked and charged by the plugin, before the actions run, so nobody is charged without getting what they paid for. With [buy], the inventory must have a free slot and BookPurchaseEvent can cancel or change the price.
  • If the player can't pay (or lacks the permission), deny-actions run instead; without them, a message.
  • Without Vault or an economy plugin, MONEY can't be paid and the console says so.

docs.title: Placeholders
docs.text:
Where Placeholders Everywhere <player>, <menu>, <page>, <pages>, <count> (enchantments in the list), <argument>, <filter>, <filter-id> Rarity menus <rarity> (name, "All" for all), <rarity-id> List items and enchantment menus <name>, <id>, <slug> (name to type), <rarity>, <rarity-id>, <max-level> (roman), <max-level-number>, <applicable>, <conflicts>, <description> Items with cost / [buy] <cost>; <rarity> and <books> (enchantments it can give)

A lore line containing <description> is repeated for each description line, keeping its format ("<gray> » <description>"); descriptions use the values of the maximum level. With PlaceholderAPI installed (optional), its %placeholders% work in every text and command. Their values are inserted as plain text (a player's nickname can't add formatting), and in [console] commands spaces become _ so a value can't add extra arguments.

docs.title: Opening menus
docs.text:
• /ce shop (permission complexenchants.shop), /ce shop <player>.
  • /ce menu open <menu> [player] [argument] [page], /ce menu list (staff, console, NPCs; skips the menu's permission).
  • A menu's own command:, or [open] from another menu (they check the menu's permission).
  • API: api.openMenu(player, "enchant_list", "epic"), api.openShop(player).

docs.title: PlaceholderAPI placeholders
docs.text:
With PlaceholderAPI installed, ComplexEnchants adds its own placeholders for scoreboards, TAB, holograms or any plugin that reads them. Both %complexenchants_…% and the short %ce_…% work. Texts come with classic colours (§); add _plain at the end for no colours (%ce_hand_list_plain%). true/false use PlaceholderAPI's boolean format.

The player's items — <slot> is hand, offhand, helmet, chestplate, leggings or boots:

Placeholder Value %ce_<slot>_count% custom enchantments on that item %ce_<slot>_list% their names with level, separated by commas %ce_<slot>_slots_used% / _slots_max% / _slots_free% enchantment slots %ce_<slot>_level_<enchant>% level of that enchantment on the item (0 if it doesn't have it) %ce_<slot>_has_<enchant>% whether it has it %ce_book_success% / %ce_book_destroy% chances of the book in hand (empty if it isn't one) %ce_equipped_count% custom enchantments on everything the player holds and wears

Enchantments (no player needed): %ce_enchant_<enchant>_name%, _rarity%, _max_level%, _applicable%, _description% (values at the max level); %ce_count% (active enchantments), %ce_rarity_<rarity>_count%.

Effects: %ce_var_<name>% (player variable), %ce_mark_<name>%, %ce_cooldown_<enchant>% and %ce_skill_cooldown_<enchant>% (seconds left, 0 = ready), %ce_in_combat%.

<enchant> is the id (life_bolt), the written name (asesino_feroz) or a vanilla one (minecraft:sharpness). Offline players get an empty value for what needs a player.

docs.title: Effects
docs.text: What enchantments do: damage bonuses, potions, area mining, auto-smelt, permanent speed… Effects live in each enchantment's file and are applied with /ce reload (no restart needed).

docs.title: Quick example
docs.text:
# enchants/life_bolt.yml (the base options: see Creating an enchantment)
name: "Life Bolt"
rarity: epic
max-level: 5
applicable: [swords]
description:
  - "<gray>+<value:1:percent>% damage against weakened players"

effects:
  # +10% damage per level against players below half health, 15-25% of the time.
  - effect: damage_bonus
    trigger: melee_attack
    percent: "10 * level"
    chance: "15 + 2 * level"
    cooldown: 2
    conditions:
      - victim_type: [player]
      - victim_health_below: 50%

  # Slows the victim down.
  - effect: potion
    trigger: melee_attack
    target: victim
    potion: slowness
    duration: "1 + 0.5 * level"

  # While held: +5% speed per level.
  - effect: attribute
    attribute: movement_speed
    operation: multiply
    amount: "0.05 * level"

docs.title: Anatomy of an effect
docs.text:
Key Meaning effect Which effect (reference). Required. trigger When it runs (triggers). Required, except for passive effects, which take none. target Who it applies to (targets), for effects that use one. chance Chance in % (formula). Default 100. cooldown Seconds before it can run again, per player and per effect. It may only depend on level. cooldown-message true = show the remaining time in the action bar when it's on cooldown. conditions All must be true (conditions). levels Exact values for specific levels: levels: { 5: { chance: 100 } }. Any argument, chance or cooldown. every Only for the interval trigger: every how many seconds (minimum 1). other keys The effect's own arguments (percent, potion…).

Errors never half-run an effect. If an effect has an error (unknown effect, a trigger it can't use, a wrong formula, a broken condition…), that whole effect is skipped and the console says exactly where and why; the rest keeps working. Unknown keys and out-of-range values are only warnings.

The order of checks when a trigger happens is: cooldown → conditions → chance → targets → effect. If an effect does not run, its cooldown is not used up.

docs.title: Where an enchantment is active
docs.text:
Effects only work while the item is worn or held in the right place. A sword in a chest or in your backpack does nothing, and enchanted books never do. Set it with active-in in the enchantment file:

active-in Active when the item is in… MAINHAND the main hand OFFHAND the off hand HANDS either hand ARMOR its armour slot ANY a hand or an armour slot

If you leave it out it's deduced from applicable: armour → ARMOR, shields → HANDS, the rest → MAINHAND. Each piece counts on its own: the same enchantment on 4 armour pieces runs 4 times (so "15% reduction" on each piece = 60%).

docs.title: Formulas and levels
docs.text:
Any number can be a formula: "10 + 5 * level", "min(level, 3)", "victim_health / victim_max_health < 0.3".

  • Operators: + - * / % ^, parentheses, comparisons < <= > >= == !=, and && || ! (true = 1, false = 0).
  • Functions: min, max, floor, ceil, round, abs, sqrt, clamp(value, min, max), random(a, b), nearby_players(radius) (players nearby, not you), nearby_entities(radius) (living entities nearby, not you) and nearby_enemies(radius) (players nearby you could hurt right now: protections, PvP zones, factions and teams are asked, like a real hit, without hitting anyone); max radius 32; var("name") (your variable as a number), mark_time("name") (seconds left on one of your marks) and cooldown("enchant") (cooldown seconds you have left on that enchantment). Random, nearby, variable, mark and cooldown functions can't be used in passive effects.
  • Variables:
Variable Available level always health, max_health, food, player_level, y every trigger (they are the player's) damage triggers with damage victim_health, victim_max_health triggers with a victim attacker_health, attacker_max_health triggers with an attacker distance triggers with a victim or an attacker speed always: your real speed in blocks/s (walking ~4.3, sprinting ~5.6, riding, falling…), measured from your positions over the last quarter of a second; standing still = 0 fall_distance always: blocks you have been falling (the mace's smash attack needs more than 1.5) forward_speed, side_speed always: your real horizontal speed (like speed) towards where you look (negative = backwards) and sideways (positive = to your right), in blocks/s victim_armor_pieces triggers with a victim: armour pieces they wear (0–4; elytra or a pumpkin don't count) potion_amplifier, potion_duration potion_gain: amplifier (0 = level I) and duration in seconds (infinite: -1) of the incoming effect

Using a variable the trigger doesn't have is an error when loading, and the message lists the ones that exist there. A result that isn't a number (division by zero…) counts as 0. Formulas that only use level are calculated once when loading, so in game they cost the same as a plain number.

docs.title: Conditions
docs.text:
Each condition is one line name: value. All must be true; use any: (at least one) and not: for other logic:

conditions:
  - health_below: 30%
  - any:
      - in_water: true
      - y_between: "-64-40"
  - not:
      sneaking: true
Condition Value Needs health_below, health_above amount (6) or % of max health (50%) — victim_health_below, victim_health_above same victim attacker_health_below, attacker_health_above same attacker victim_type, attacker_type list of entity types, tags ("#minecraft:undead") or mob, monster, animal victim / attacker victim_is_boss true / false (Wither, Ender Dragon) victim attacker_holding, victim_holding list of items or tags in the attacker's / victim's main hand attacker / victim has_potion, victim_has_potion, attacker_has_potion list of active potion effects (any of them) — / victim / attacker potion_type list of potion effects: the incoming one is one of them potion_gain trigger damage_cause list of damage causes (fall, lava, fly_into_wall, projectile…) or groups: fire (fire, lava, magma block, campfire), explosion damage is_projectile, critical, headshot true / false: the damage comes from a projectile, is a critical hit, the projectile hit the head damage sneaking, sprinting, on_ground, in_water, underwater, on_fire, blocking, gliding, using_item, charging true / false (underwater = head under water; using_item = holding use on an item: charging a spear, drawing a bow, eating, shield up…; charging = charging a spear and the charge is still active: once the spear "gets tired", it stops counting even if you keep holding) — in_world list of world names; * matches any text ("dungeon_*") — in_biome list of biomes — time day / night — weather clear / rain / thunder — y_between range: "0-64" or [0, 64] — light_below, light_above number 0–15 — block_type list of blocks or tags ("#minecraft:logs") block block_natural true / false: no player placed the block (blocks that existed before this version count as natural; pistons and falling sand/gravel keep the mark) block crop_grown true / false: the block is a fully grown crop (wheat, carrots, potatoes, beetroots, nether wart, cocoa, sweet berries) block holding list of item groups (from item-groups.yml) held in the main hand — consumed_item list of items or tags (golden_apple, "#minecraft:...") consume trigger has_permission list of permissions (needs all) — level_above, food_above number — in_combat true / false — in_zone list of zones (from zone; any of them) — has_mark, victim_has_mark, attacker_has_mark list of marks (any of them) — / victim / attacker var_is variables and their value: { mode: tank, stacks: 3 } (all must match; unset = 0) — expression formula; true if it isn't 0 —

docs.title: Debugging: /ce debug
docs.text:
/ce debug (permission complexenchants.command.debug, op) shows in your chat every one of your effects that runs, or why it didn't: cooldown (seconds left), the condition that failed, the chance roll, no target, or another plugin cancelling it. Run it again to turn it off.

To show variables, marks, cooldowns or combat on a scoreboard or TAB, use the PlaceholderAPI placeholders %ce_var_<name>%, %ce_mark_<name>%, %ce_cooldown_<enchant>%, %ce_skill_cooldown_<enchant>% and %ce_in_combat% (README).

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Players only: mobs wearing enchanted items don't run effects (yet).
  • interval runs once per second (every 1 at least; a decimal waits for the next whole second). Changes like forward_speed or a spear getting tired can take up to a second to be noticed.
  • Plugins that change damage after ComplexEnchants (HIGHEST/MONITOR) change its result. ComplexEnchants applies damage at HIGH and never at MONITOR, on purpose.
  • Permanent potions are recognised by their signature (infinite, ambient, no particles). If another plugin gives exactly the same kind of potion, removing the item could remove it too. It's unlikely; use attribute when there is one (speed, health…).
  • Particles that need extra data (colour, block) aren't supported yet.
  • Folia: an effect on an entity or place in another region (a nearby target far away) is applied one tick later, in that region's thread. Area/vein blocks in another region are skipped.

docs.title: Effect groups
docs.text:
Each effect rolls its own chance and has its own cooldown. To make several effects happen together or not at all (+50 % damage and slowness on the same roll), or to build sequences with delays, group them:

effects:
  - effect: group
    trigger: projectile_attack
    chance: "11 + level"       # ONE roll for the whole group
    cooldown: "9 - level"      # ONE cooldown for the whole group
    conditions:                # checked once
      - victim_type: [player]
    effects:
      - effect: damage_bonus
        percent: "40 + 10 * level"
      - effect: potion
        target: victim
        potion: slowness
        amplifier: 4
        duration: "level"
      - effect: sound
        sound: entity.ghast.scream
        delay: 0.5             # wait 0.5 s before this effect and the ones after it
  • The group has trigger, chance, cooldown, cooldown-message, conditions and levels (and every with interval). Its effects do not take trigger, chance, cooldown or every (load error).
  • Each effect in the group can have its own target, conditions (they only filter that effect), levels and a delay in seconds. Delays add up: 60 s in total at most.
  • Effects that change the event itself (damage_bonus and the other damage effects, cancel_event, drops, experience, mining) can't come after a delay: the event is over by then (load error).
  • After a delay, if you disconnect or die, the rest doesn't run; if a step's target no longer exists (it died or despawned), that step is skipped. /ce reload cancels pending delays.
  • Formulas use the values from the moment of the trigger (damage, health…), even after a delay.
  • If an effect in the group has an error, the whole group is discarded. A group can't contain another group.
  • In /ce debug and <value:…>, step 3 of group 2 is 2.3.

docs.title: Reusable groups: effect-groups.yml
docs.text:
A group used by several enchantments is written once in effect-groups.yml and used with use::

# effect-groups.yml
stun:
  - effect: potion
    target: victim
    potion: slowness
    amplifier: 3
    duration: "1 + level"
  - effect: sound
    sound: entity.iron_golem.hurt

# enchants/hammer.yml
effects:
  - effect: group
    trigger: melee_attack
    chance: "5 * level"
    use: stun

Each enchantment that uses it compiles it with its trigger and its levels (level is that enchantment's level). If a group doesn't fit an enchantment's trigger, the error says which one: effect-groups.yml (enchants/hammer.yml).

docs.title: How damage is calculated
docs.text:
All damage effects of one hit (the attacker's and the victim's) only note their part, and the damage is calculated once, always in this order:

base damage
+ add_damage
× (1 + bonus)          sum of damage_bonus
× (1 − reduction)      sum of damage_reduction (capped)
− negate_damage
never below 0

Minecraft's armour, Protection and Resistance then apply as usual. The result never depends on the order of the effects. In config.yml:

damage:
  bonus-stacking: ADD        # ADD: they add up (15% × 4 = 60%). MULTIPLY: like other plugins.
  reduction-stacking: ADD
  max-bonus: ""              # empty = no cap
  max-reduction: 75%         # the reduction can never go above 100% (damage never heals)

Damage dealt by effects (damage, lightning, bleed) is normal Minecraft damage, so protections and PvP settings see it, but it never triggers more effects: two players with "thorns" never bounce damage back and forth forever.

docs.title: Tools: area, vein and drops
docs.text:
• Which blocks an area or vein breaks: blocks your tool mines properly, never unbreakable ones (bedrock), and at most twice as hard as the one you mined. Mining stone also breaks the ores around it, but not obsidian.
  • Protections decide block by block: each extra block is broken as if you broke it yourself (it passes protections, uses durability and drops normally). If a protection cancels the block you mined, nothing else breaks.
  • Limit: at most tools.max-blocks blocks per action, counting the one you mined, nearest first (config.yml, default 64, absolute limit 512). The console warns when loading if a level could go over.
  • Drops are always applied in this order: multiply → smelt → collect (telekinesis), whatever the order you write them in.

docs.title: Passive effects
docs.text:
Passive effects (attribute, permanent_potion) take no trigger: they're on while the item is active.

  • Attribute changes are never saved on the player, so a crash can't leave "ghost" bonuses.
  • Permanent potions come back after milk, a totem or /effect clear, and after respawning. They're removed when you log out and cleaned up on join if a crash left one behind. A stronger potion from another source (beacon, potion) is never removed.
  • Their values can only depend on level (no random): they're calculated when you equip the item.

docs.title: Values in the description
docs.text:
The description can show an effect's values for the item's level, so you never have to write numbers twice:

description:
  - "<gray>+<value:1:percent>% damage (<value:1:chance>% chance)"

<value:N:argument>: N is the effect's number in the list (from 1, as in /ce debug; inside a group, <value:1.2:duration> is the group's second effect); chance and cooldown also work. If the value depends on the game ("damage * 0.1") the formula is shown; if the tag is wrong, ?.

Calculations with those values: inside <calc:…>, value(N, argument) is the same number, so you can do maths with it:

description:
  - "<gray>Up to <white><calc:value(1, percent) * 5>%</white> with 5 stacks"

If the value depends on the game, the whole <calc> shows ?.

Incompatible enchantments: <conflicts> lists them, by name and in their colour (its conflicts: plus the ones that name it). A description line with <conflicts> and nothing to list is removed.

docs.title: Effects reference
docs.text: Arguments with a value in brackets are optional; that's their default.

docs.title: Combat
docs.text:
Effect Arguments Target Notes damage_bonus percent — +% damage. Damage triggers. add_damage amount — + flat damage. damage_reduction percent — −% damage received. negate_damage amount — − flat damage received. lifesteal percent — Heals that % of the final damage you deal. melee_attack, projectile_attack. heal amount self damage amount, [bypass-armor: false] victim Deals damage (protections and PvP are respected). bypass-armor: true = magic damage: armor neither reduces it nor wears out (totems still save). potion potion, duration (s), [amplifier: 0], [particles: true] self Amplifier 0 = level I. remove_potion potion self Removes that potion effect from the target. ignite duration (s) victim lightning [damage: false] victim Visual only; with damage: true it deals 5 damage to the target only (no fire, nobody else). knockback [strength: 1], [vertical: auto] victim Pushes away from you (0.6 per point of strength); negative pulls. vertical: how high it lifts them (auto: 0.15–0.3; 0 = flat); it never adds to the lift they already have, such as a hit's. bleed damage, [interval: 1] (s), [times: 3] victim Stops if the target dies. set_damage amount — The base damage becomes this; the other damage effects apply after it. freeze duration (s), [lock: true] victim Frozen like in powder snow: slow and, fully frozen, damage. lock: true = maxed for duration; lock: false = that many seconds of freezing that thaw by themselves (like AE's SCREEN_FREEZE). explode [power: 2] (TNT = 4, max 8), [fire: false], [break-blocks: false] victim Never hurts you; with break-blocks, protections decide. pumpkin_head duration (s) victim Players only. Their helmet always comes back (when it ends, on quit, on death, after a crash).

The first five go through the damage calculation.

docs.text: Effect Arguments Triggers Notes area_mining [radius: 1], [depth: 0], [blocks: any] mine_block A (2r+1)² wall in front of you; looking up/down, a floor. depth adds layers. blocks limits which blocks it breaks (crops only, for example). plant_seeds [radius: 1] (max 5), [seeds: any] triggers with a block Plants on the free farmland (and nether wart on soul sand) around the block, with the seeds in your inventory. Protections decide each one. vein_mining [max: 16], [blocks: any] mine_block Connected blocks of the same type, also diagonally. blocks limits which veins (blocks or tags). autosmelt — block_drops, kill Uses the server's furnace recipes (datapacks included). telekinesis — block_drops, kill Drops to your inventory (with kill, the experience too). What doesn't fit stays on the ground. multiply_drops [multiplier: 2], [blocks: any] block_drops, kill Decimals are a chance: ×1.5 on 3 items gives 4 or 5. xp_multiplier multiplier mine_block, kill, fish

docs.text: Effect Arguments Notes attribute attribute, amount, [operation: add] add, multiply_base or multiply. Speed, max health, armour, damage, reach… permanent_potion potion, [amplifier: 0] Infinite, no particles.

docs.text:
Effect Arguments Target message text self actionbar text self title title, [subtitle: ""], [fade-in: 0.5], [stay: 2], [fade-out: 0.5] (s) self sound sound, [volume: 1], [pitch: 1] self particle particle, [count: 10], [spread: 0.5] self command command, [as: console] (console or player) self (once per target) cancel_event — (cancellable triggers) — repair amount — (the enchanted item) damage_item amount — (the enchanted item) give_xp amount self mark name, duration (s) self remove_mark name self set_var name, value (formula) or text (text), [persistent: true] — add_var name, amount, [persistent: true] — reset_cooldown [enchant: this one] — temp_attribute attribute, amount, duration (s), [operation: add] self drop_item item, [amount: 1] self (or block, victim…) repair_armor, damage_armor [amount: 0], [percent: 0], [slot: all] (all, head, chest, legs, feet) self cancel_armor_damage — — remove_enchant [enchant: this one] — velocity [strength: 1], [direction: look] (look, up, forward), [add: true], [no-fall: false] self temp_block block, [radius: 0] (max 5), duration (s) self jail block, [shape: cuboid] (cuboid, sphere), [radius: 3], [height: 3], [roof: true], duration (s) victim zone name, [shape: circle] (circle, square), radius, duration (s), [particle] self launch_projectile [entity: arrow], [speed: 3], [fuse: 4], [break-blocks: false] — replace_projectile [entity: arrow], [fuse: 4], [break-blocks: false] — bossbar id, text, [color: white], [style: solid], [progress: 1], [duration: 0] self bossbar_remove id self
  • Text (message, actionbar, title) is MiniMessage with <player>, <target>, <victim>, <attacker>, <level> and <var:name> (one of your variables).
  • command has the same placeholders as plain text. For mobs, <victim>, <attacker> and <target> are their UUID, never their name: a custom name can't sneak arguments into a console command.
  • particle only accepts particles without extra data (no dust or block for now).
  • Unbreaking-like: cancel_event with the item_damage trigger and a chance. It only protects the item that has the enchantment.

docs.title: Active skills
docs.text:
An enchantment with effects using trigger: active_skill is a skill: it doesn't fire by itself, the player activates it.

# enchants/domain.yml
active-skill:
  cooldown: "65 - 5 * level"         # seconds (can only depend on level)
  requirements:                      # optional; checked in order
    - condition: { health_above: 50% }
      message: "<red>You need more than half your health."
effects:
  - effect: zone
    trigger: active_skill
    name: domain
    radius: 16
    duration: 8
  • How to activate them:
  • with the skill book (/ce give skillbook <players> [amount]): right-click and a menu opens with your skills, their level and cooldown;
  • with the key in skills.keybind (config.yml): sneak_swap (sneak + swap hands key, F), swap (just F) or none. With one skill available it is activated; with several, the menu opens. skills.keybind-requires-book can make the key need the book too: false (it always works), hotbar (the book in the hotbar or the other hand: the same slot it costs Bedrock players, who can't use the keys) or inventory (anywhere in the inventory). Without the book, the key does what it normally does. The plugin's default configuration uses hotbar.
  • Which skills you have: those of the items in your hands, armour and hotbar (with the book in your hand, the sword still counts). Outside their slot, effects that touch "the enchanted item" (repair, damage_item, remove_enchant) act on what you hold.
  • Before activating, in this order: silence, the skill's cooldown and requirements. If something fails, the player gets the message and nothing else happens (no cooldown is spent).
  • Silence: anyone with the skills.silence-mark mark (silenced by default, set with a mark effect) can't use skills.
  • A skill's effects can also have their own conditions, chance and cooldown, like any other effect.
# config.yml
skills:
  keybind: sneak_swap
  keybind-requires-book: hotbar   # false | hotbar | inventory
  silence-mark: silenced
  book:
    material: book
    name: "<gold><bold>Skill Book"
    lore: ["<gray>Right-click to see your skills."]
  menu-title: "<dark_gray>⚔ Active Skills"

docs.title: Targets
docs.text:
target Who self you (default for most effects) victim the entity you hit or killed attacker whoever hit or killed you nearby entities around you (not you), nearest first block the block of the trigger (sounds, particles, lightning)

nearby takes options:

target:
  type: nearby
  radius: 6          # blocks, 0.5–32 (default 5)
  max: 5             # entities, 1–64 (default 10)
  entities: [monster]   # optional filter (see victim_type below)

If the target doesn't exist in that event (a death with no attacker), the effect doesn't run.

docs.title: Triggers
docs.text:
Trigger When Offers melee_attack you hit something in melee damage, victim, cancellable projectile_attack your arrow/trident hits something. The enchantments of the weapon that launched it count (even if it is no longer in your hand, like a thrown trident), plus your armour's damage, victim, cancellable take_damage you take any damage damage, cancellable take_entity_damage a mob or player damages you damage, attacker, cancellable fall_damage you take fall damage damage, cancellable kill you kill something victim, drops, experience death you die attacker (if there is one) mine_block you break a block (only the one you break: the extra blocks of an area or a vein don't fire it; their drops do go through block_drops) block, experience, cancellable block_drops a block you broke drops its items block, drops shoot you shoot a bow or crossbow cancellable shield_block you block with a shield damage (read only: the hit before the shield), attacker, cancellable item_damage the enchanted item loses durability cancellable fish you catch something experience, cancellable consume you eat or drink cancellable sneak you start sneaking — jump you jump cancellable right_click you right-click with the main hand clicked block (if any), cancellable interval every every seconds while the item is active — fatal_damage a hit is about to kill you (fully calculated); cancelling it saves you (and no totem is used) damage (read only), attacker if any, cancellable totem_use a totem is used (cancelling it = it doesn't save you) cancellable hunger_loss, hunger_gain your hunger goes down / up cancellable projectile_launch you launch any projectile (arrow, trident, pearl, snowball…) cancellable combat_enter, combat_leave you enter / leave combat (see combat: in config.yml) — world_change you change worlds — block_place you place a block block, cancellable projectile_hit_block your projectile hits a block (the weapon that launched it counts) block shield_disable your shield gets disabled (by an axe, for example) attacker, cancellable item_break the enchanted item is about to break with this wear; cancelling it saves it cancellable active_skill the player activates the skill (active skills) — potion_gain a potion effect is about to be applied to you (new, renewed or stronger), from any source; removing it or it running out doesn't count. With cancel_event it isn't applied potion, cancellable

Effects and conditions that need something the trigger doesn't offer are rejected when loading, with the list of triggers that would work. Triggers react only if the event wasn't cancelled by another plugin (protections, claims…).

docs.title: Creating an enchantment
docs.text:
Copy enchants/_example.yml (files starting with _ are not loaded) and rename it. The file name is the id: life_bolt.yml becomes complexenchants:life_bolt. Use only lowercase letters, numbers and _.

enabled: true
name: "Life Bolt"                 # the rarity colour is added automatically
description:
  - "<gray>Strikes with the power of life."
rarity: epic                      # from rarities.yml
max-level: 3
applicable: [swords, axes]        # item groups from item-groups.yml
conflicts: [other_enchant, minecraft:sharpness]
mode: INHERIT                     # BOOKS | VANILLA | INHERIT
anvil-cost: 4
sources:                          # VANILLA sources (each also needs its switch in config.yml)
  enchanting-table: true
  villagers: true
  loot: true
  fishing: false
book-chances:                     # BOOKS mode: "50", "40-80" or "random" (destroy = 100 − success)
  success: "40-80"

The template documents every option.

Never delete an enchantment that players already have. Set enabled: false instead. If you do delete a file, ComplexEnchants remembers the enchantment (data/known-enchants.yml) and keeps it registered, so items that have it are not broken; it shows as "removed" in their lore.

docs.title: In-game editor
docs.text:
/ce editor (permission complexenchants.editor, op) edits the same files without leaving the game: chest menus to move around and Minecraft's own forms (dialogs, 1.21.6+) to edit. Its start screen has four buttons:

  • Enchantments: every enchantment (disabled ones in grey, "waiting for a restart" marked), by rarity and id, with a rarity filter, a search (id or name) and files that failed to load at the end (click: their problems). Click one to open it:
  • Properties: name, description, rarity, max level, applicable groups, conflicts, where it is active.
  • Sources and book: mode, the four sources, book success chance, weight, anvil cost, grindstone.
  • Effects: one item per effect. Click to edit, Shift + left/right click to move it, right click to remove it. "Add" asks for the effect, then the trigger (only compatible ones), then its form. Moving or removing an effect renumbers the <value:N:…> tags of the description.
  • Enable/disable, duplicate (asks for the new id) and its warnings.
  • Create (in the list): id, name, description, rarity, max level and groups. The file only has that; the rest comes from its rarity.
  • Rarities, Item groups and Vanilla enchantments: the same forms for rarities.yml, item-groups.yml and vanilla-enchants.yml. A rarity or group in use can't be removed (it says who uses it); "Reset" removes a vanilla enchantment's section, so it is like in Minecraft again.

Every change is checked with the real loaders before saving: with errors, the form opens again with them and with what you wrote. Saving writes the file (a copy of the previous one goes to backups/editor/, the last 10 per file) and applies it like /ce reload; what needs a restart is marked ⏻. If someone changed the file since you opened it, nothing is overwritten and you are told. Nothing is deleted from the editor: to remove an enchantment, use its file.

Advanced parts are shown read-only and kept as they are when you save the rest: effect groups with steps or delays, levels:, any:/not: conditions, named groups (use:), active-skill and targets with options. A file saved from the editor keeps its comments, but its style may change (quotes, lists).

The editor is as powerful as the console: the command effect runs console commands. Give complexenchants.editor only to trusted admins. Bedrock players (Geyser) don't see dialogs properly.
